title: Commitment Hierarchies under Intent Revision: A Belief-Revision Account of Salvage in Tool-Use Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.37453v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a user changes their mind partway through a task, an agent that has already split the task into sub-goals and paid for tool calls must decide, per cached sub-result, whether to keep, patch, or discard it (salvage), restarting wastes valid work and continuing unchanged answers the old question. Our main finding is that salvage quality is a matter of role design rather than model capability: a language model asked the keep/patch/discard question one node at a time is unreliable, but asked to classify the revision once, with a deterministic layer propagating the decision, it reaches the cost-optimal oracle on all three models tested, from two vendors. Modeling the plan as a commitment hierarchy and the intent change as a belief-revision operator with AGM style postulates, we prove that no policy observing only a node's local view can be both safe and cost optimal, while the single classification design is both. Across three environment

translated_title: 意图修订下的承诺层级：工具使用智能体中“抢救复用”的信念修正解释
translated_abstract: 当用户在任务中途改变主意时，一个已经将任务拆分为子目标并支付了工具调用成本的智能体，必须针对每个缓存的子结果决定是保留、修补还是丢弃（即“抢救复用”，salvage）——全部重启会浪费有效的工作，而一成不变地继续则回答的是旧的问题。我们的主要发现是：抢救复用的质量取决于角色设计而非模型能力：让语言模型逐节点地回答保留/修补/丢弃问题是不可靠的，但如果让模型对修订进行一次分类，再由一个确定性层传播该决策，则在测试的全部三个模型（来自两家厂商）上都能达到成本最优的神谕水平。我们将计划建模为承诺层级，将意图变化建模为符合 AGM 风格公设的信念修正算子，并证明：任何只观察节点局部视角的策略都无法同时做到安全与成本最优，而单次分类设计则两者兼备。在三个环境中……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将用户中途改变意图时智能体对缓存子结果的“保留/修补/丢弃”决策建模为承诺层级上的信念修正问题，从理论上证明仅凭节点局部视角的策略无法同时做到安全与成本最优，并提出让模型一次性分类意图修订、再由确定性层传播决策的设计，从而在多个模型上达到成本最优的神谕水平——表明抢救复用质量取决于角色设计而非模型能力。
en_tdlr: The paper models salvage decisions (keep/patch/discard) over cached sub-results under mid-task intent revision as belief revision on a commitment hierarchy, proves that no policy observing only a node's local view can be both safe and cost-optimal, and shows that a single revision classification propagated by a deterministic layer reaches the cost-optimal oracle across models—demonstrating that salvage quality is a matter of role design rather than model capability.
